items.title: The full orthogonal group has a unique Haar probability

source.anchor: Section2 first paragraph; AppendixB2.1 row-reflection invariance; Section4.1 Haar eigenbasis draw
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS explicates the standard Haar background invoked by the source.

items.statement: For every natural finite dimension n, the full real orthogonal group O(n), with its inherited matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra, has exactly one measure which is both a probability and a Haar measure. This explicates the standard Haar background invoked in the source.
assumptions: n is an arbitrary natural finite dimension. The paper applications use n>=3 or d>=2; the shared background also covers n=0.
O(n) is the full real orthogonal group O^T O=I, equipped with the subspace topology of finite real matrices and its Borel sigma-algebra. Both determinant signs are allowed whenever they exist.

Haar means left invariant, finite on compact sets and positive on nonempty open sets. Probability means total mass one. Compactness and second countability are proved internally, not assumed as public premises.

obligations.label: The full orthogonal group has a unique Haar probability

bindings.boundary: Only the common full orthogonal Haar probability and fixed left multiplication invariance. Determinant-conditioned laws, component half-mass, principal-minor sign/zero expectation, Gaussian densities, independence from an algorithm seed, adaptive posterior invariance, Krylov reduction and both main lower bounds remain open. Dimension zero is included as a singleton group; no two-components claim is made there.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper invokes full orthogonal Haar probability in dimension n>=3 or d>=2 and uses fixed row-reflection invariance.
assumption_deltas.lean: All natural finite dimensions, canonical Borel full group, actual Haar constructor. The n=0 case is a singleton; no determinant component or conditional law is asserted.
assumption_deltas.reason: Standard background is expanded and proved internally. This disclosed dimension extension does not strengthen the paper conclusions or identify the two experiments beyond their common full Haar law.

items.statement: For every natural finite dimension n and every fixed Q in the full real orthogonal group O(n), the pushforward of the constructed Haar probability by O -> Q O equals that same probability. This includes a fixed single-row reflection.
assumptions: n is an arbitrary natural finite dimension. The paper applications use n>=3 or d>=2; the shared background also covers n=0.
O(n) is the full real orthogonal group O^T O=I, equipped with the subspace topology of finite real matrices and its Borel sigma-algebra. Both determinant signs are allowed whenever they exist.

Haar means left invariant, finite on compact sets and positive on nonempty open sets. Probability means total mass one. Compactness and second countability are proved internally, not assumed as public premises.
Q is any fixed real orthogonal n by n matrix.
